name: A42 Section 8.10 (new subsection after 8.9)
new:
### 8.10 A curvature-squared term

The audit's failure has a clear signature: chains started rough stay rough, while chains started flat stay smooth. A term in the square of the curvature penalizes the spikes a rough start contains, and quantum matter on curved spacetime requires such a term: the logarithmic divergence of its stress tensor is removed by a counterterm quadratic in the Riemann tensor (Utiyama and DeWitt, 1962). Hamber's lattice form adds $a δ_h^2 A_h^2/V_h$ on each triangle h, with $V_h$ a tenth of the volume of the simplices that share it, and at a = 0.005 the critical coupling becomes $k_c = 0.2443(11)$ (Hamber, 1993). The rerun engine is the audited engine with this one term. With a = 0 it reproduces the audited engine's histories and final configurations byte for byte; with a = 0.005 its running totals agree with full recomputation after every sweep to better than one part in $10^{12}$, and a flat start carries no curvature-squared energy.

The rerun repeats the Section 8.9 protocol with a = 0.005 in all 24 main chains: the same seeds, the same six rough preparations at k = 0.1 without the term, and the same 3,000 equilibration and 12,000 measurement sweeps.

| L | k | Flat-start mean R | Rough-start mean R | Split R-hat | Screen | Split R-hat without the term |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 0.05 | -0.2762 | -0.2717 | 1.004 | passes | 1.573 |
| 3 | 0.065 | -0.2649 | -0.2665 | 1.006 | passes | 13.032 |
| 4 | 0.05 | -0.2751 | -0.2737 | 1.003 | passes | 5.498 |
| 4 | 0.065 | -0.2616 | -0.2621 | 1.004 | passes | 17.716 |

All four groups pass the screen, where all four failed without the term. Rough starts enter the flat-start band within 500 of the 3,000 equilibration sweeps, the start classes differ by at most 1.4 standard errors of their seed means, and effective sample sizes reach 140 to 334 per chain, against 3 to 29 without the term. The scaling identity holds to within 0.08 percent in every chain.

![Rerun with the curvature-squared term, a = 0.005. Each curve averages 100 sweeps; flat starts solid, rough starts dashed. Gray shading marks equilibration sweeps, and the first rough-start values lie above the axis.](regge_r2_audit.png)

Near the shifted transition mixing slows. A 3⁴ scan from both starts finds the average curvature rising from -0.24 at k = 0.10 through zero between k = 0.24 and 0.26, beside Hamber's $k_c$, and a shorter 4⁴ scan crosses zero in the same interval. The same design, shortened to 2,000 and 6,000 sweeps, passes the screen at k = 0.20 on 3⁴ and 4⁴ (split R-hat 1.013 and 1.023) and at k = 0.24 on 3⁴ (1.047), where the start classes still differ by 2.5 standard errors of their seed means; on 4⁴ at k = 0.24 it fails (1.077), with the start classes within 0.8 standard errors, and effective sample sizes fall to 17 to 84 per chain. Continued for 12,000 more sweeps from their final configurations, those six chains give split R-hat 1.029, inside the screen. Past $k_c$, at k = 0.30 on 3⁴, the two starts begin to differ.

Hamber (1992) found his estimated critical exponents independent of a, and that the theories with and without the term may share a phase, which would give them a common unitary continuum limit. The term also bounds the action below. Completing the square on each triangle gives $I \ge (λ - k^2/4a) Σ_s V_s$, positive for k below $2\sqrt{aλ} ≈ 0.141$, which covers both audit couplings; whether the integral over degenerate configurations converges is still open, and the bound stops short of $k_c$. The term has costs. Its Weyl-squared part brings a massive spin-2 ghost in perturbation theory (Stelle, 1977); lattices of 3⁴ and 4⁴ sites leave finite-size scaling, the critical exponent and a Newtonian potential to larger runs; and writing the term into the specification would add about 350 bits, 16,624 in place of 16,272.

![Average curvature against k with the curvature-squared term, a = 0.005: a 3⁴ scan and a shorter 4⁴ scan from flat and rough starts, with the group means of the 3⁴ and 4⁴ reruns. The dotted line marks Hamber's k_c = 0.2443; the shaded band is where the action is bounded below.](regge_r2_scan.png)

name: A42 Conclusion
old: The independent Regge audit fails the prespecified mixing screen in all four parameter groups, so the sampled regime is not established as an equilibrated smooth phase.
new: The independent Regge audit fails the prespecified mixing screen in all four parameter groups, so the sampled regime is not established as an equilibrated smooth phase. **With a curvature-squared term, which quantum matter requires, the same audit passes in all four, and the average curvature rises to zero beside the known critical coupling, where mixing slows.**
plain_new: The independent Regge audit fails the prespecified mixing screen in all four parameter groups, so the sampled regime is not established as an equilibrated smooth phase. With a curvature-squared term, which quantum matter requires, the same audit passes in all four, and the average curvature rises to zero beside the known critical coupling, where mixing slows.

name: A42 Abstract
old: All four groups in a new 24-chain Regge audit fail the mixing screen; a complete quantum-gravity construction remains open.
new: All four groups in a new 24-chain Regge audit fail the mixing screen; **adding a curvature-squared term, which quantum matter requires, makes all four pass. A** complete quantum-gravity construction remains open.
plain_new: All four groups in a new 24-chain Regge audit fail the mixing screen; adding a curvature-squared term, which quantum matter requires, makes all four pass. A complete quantum-gravity construction remains open.
